 Nonsensory is the third game to be announced for The Jackbox Party Pack 9 , revealed on June 13th, 2022. Nonsensory is about writing and drawing prompts and rating said prompts based off of a given question from a 1 to 10 scale, hoping to test levels of NSP (Nonsensory Perception). Players are rewarded points by how close their response was to the correct answer.

 Gameplay [ ] 

 Tutorial [ ] 

 If the VIP chooses to take a pregame exercise, they are asked to name something that matches their prompt's secret number. The other players guess between 1 and 10, and the answer is revealed after everyone guesses.

 Round 1- Writing [ ] 

 During Round 1, players will write something like a text or a name of something. During the prompt-writing, Audience players will vote on what card matches a particular question. The more players who match, the more points the Audience gets.

 The players vote as before, swapping between prompts as players guess. Players get points the closer to the answer they were. The writer gets points if players guessed the secret number, or the numbers adjactent to it. (If 6, the numbers 5 and 7 will award points too!)

 Round 2- Drawing [ ] 

 During Round 2, players will draw something based on the prompt given, like a bug or a tree. Just like Round 1, the Audience will perform sync-ups with cards.

 Players vote like before, but at any time (even during Round 1) players can tap and hold the CONFIDENCE button to apply Confidence to your answer. Confident players will get a 1000-point bonus if they land on or next to the secret number. However, they lose 500 points if they do not land in that range!

 Round 3- Final [ ] 

 During Round 3, the points are doubled! Players are asked to draw something between two points (like DRAGON and SOFA) and the numberings have changed to be 60-100% Point A and 60-100% Point B.

 Players vote one last time, and the winner is decided by who has the most points at the end.

 The Audience will also be rewarded an Audience Rank depending on how many points they get.

 Trivia [ ] 

 If the game has less than five players, there will be four rounds instead of three.

 Outside of each test room there is a sign which reads: "SAFETY FIRST"
"[NUMBER] TESTS"
"Without a "Fart" incident"

 This sign is a live tally of how many tests the host has completed without a player using "fart" in their answer. This counter resets back to 0 if at least one player used the word "fart" in their answer in a round.

 The credit theme makes a direct reference to non-fungible tokens , a digital identifier that mints images onto the blockchain. This process makes any illustrations minted unique, and cannot be copied, substituted, or subdivided. These are worth Ethereum , a type of cryptocurrency , which can be subsequently used as currency-currency.
 More specifically, it refers to the Board Ape Yacht Club NFT, one of the most recognizable and popular series of non-fungible tokens.

 Nonsensory is a party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 9 .

 In this game, players test their NSP (Nonsensory Perception) by trying to guess the percentage or ranking (from a 1 to 10 scale) of another player's prompt or drawing, based off of a given question.

 Gameplay

 All players are shown a scale with a determined number or range ranging from one subject to another. The player will be tasked to write an answer that would make sure the other players can accurately guess their secret number. The Audience can partake in a synchronization test, where they'll be shown four cards with different shapes and symbols and ask a question, like "Which of these cards is the most extroverted?" for example.

 Once all answers are in, one of the players' responses is shown, of which the others, as well as the Audience members, will have to guess which number, percentage or stars said answer lands on the scale. Players can also tap and hold the " Confidence Button " in order to double their earnings, or lose an amount of their points. They can also press one of the three emotes shown on their device to share their feedback on the drawing.

 When all players have made their guesses, they're shown and then the real answer lights up on the scale. Players will earn 1,000 points if they're spot on, 500 if they're one away from the correct answer, and points ranging from 350 to 0 for being off.

 If a player uses their Confidence and are within the range, they'll earn double the points; however, if they use their Confidence and is out of the actual answer's range, then they'll lose 500 points.

 The second round (and third in a game with 5 or less players) works about the same, but instead of the players writing an answer, they'll have to draw a picture portraying the determined range. (If the "Writing Only" or "Drawing Only" settings are turned on, then these will override said rounds.) 

 The final round will have everyone draw a prompt with a range between two completely separate subjects (like a snake and a baseball bat) and the points are doubled this round, making the correct answer 2,000 points and its neighboring answers, 1,000. The board will also change colors from gray to orange at the top half and purple at the bottom half.

 After the final round is over, all of the final scores are shown, and the player with the most points wins the game. The Audience will also be shown a sentence regarding their performance in-game.

 Development

 The design team for the game are as follows:

 Mark Turowetz - Director

 Arnie Niekamp - Lead Editorial and Original Concept

 Ben Jacobs - Lead Gameplay Engineer

 Dave Innis - Lead Artist

 Andy Poland - Music

 Louis Hayes - QA Lead

 Steve Pakal - Game Design

 Trivia

 The game includes a sign next to the round's door that states how many tests there have been since a "fart incident." This number ticks up until someone uses the word "fart" at any point in the game, then it goes back to zero.

 Two and a half of the emotes seen in the game are taken directly from Civic Doodle : T he laughing emote, the heart emote, and the question mark emote, with an added exclamation mark to it.

 The song's lyrics make a reference to non-fungible tokens ("This chimp's not an NFT") , most likely a reference to "Bored Apes", an NFT collection consisting of cartoon apes with randomly generated traits.

 The fonts used for this game are:
 Good Grief PB , designed by Phil Bracco for Pink Broccoli. [ 1 ] 

 Aspire , designed by Jim Lyles and Brian J. Bonislawsky for Grype. (The font was inspired by the logo of car company Acura, a division of Honda.) [ 2 ] 

 Midnight Chalker , designed by David Kerkhoff for Hanoded. [ 3 ]
